title: Historical and Conditional Forecasts of Sampled Net-Position Peaks
subtitle: Common targets, source-specific results and exploratory diagnostics
abstract: We benchmark established forecasts of the 0.95 quantile of the largest absolute net position observed at issue and over the next H source records. Historical constructions are evaluated against ridge quantile regression (QR) and local quantiles using completed responses and matched-history controls. The FX evaluation archive had previously been inspected; the Treasury exercise replays a downloaded vintage by economic date rather than historical public release. On 6,625 FX origins, the declared six-record-horizon QR primary lowers mean pinball loss by 12.66% against its original rolling reference and 14.77% against a matched-history reference, with 376 breaches versus 332 and 360. On 277 weekly Treasury-aggregate origins, the separately fitted six-week QR primary raises loss by 50.79% and breaches from 28 to 54. Exploratory AR replay improves on matched increment translation in five of eight cells while breaches increase in all eight. Reweighting eight archived .95 reports distinguishes the FX short-horizon reductions in both mean error components from the small 24-record gain, which reverses above an underprediction/overprediction weight ratio of 20.63, near the stipulated 19. These retrospective comparisons establish source-, horizon-, history- and family-dependent rankings, without coverage guarantees or observed trading and funding benefits.

sections.title: 1. Introduction

blocks.html: Dealers absorb customer order imbalances while managing inventory risk and scarce balance-sheet capacity. Inventory affects optimal dealer pricing (Ho and Stoll, 1981), FX dealing (Lyons, 1995), and observed inventory adjustment in dealership markets (Hansch, Naik and Viswanathan, 1998). Treasury intermediation likewise depends on dealer capacity (Duffie et al., 2023). A forecast of the maximum recorded position magnitude over a future horizon may support monitoring of the measured position: an endpoint can return toward its starting value after an intervening large position. Translating that monitoring signal into a particular margin or financing decision requires the corresponding contractual and balance-sheet inputs.

We ask whether mature conditional estimators improve forecasts of an absolute sampled-position peak relative to simple historical constructions. Every report is evaluated against the same peak response and upper-quantile score on common issue origins. The endpoint-derived bound introduced below is a benchmark rather than a direct peak-quantile estimate. The historical alternatives use past headrooms, paths translated to the current signed position, or native peaks floored at the observed current magnitude. The conditional alternatives use ridge quantile regression, nearest-neighbor quantiles and scaled nearest-neighbor quantiles.

The matched-history FX regression comparison lowers mean loss by 14.77%, but increases breaches from 360 to 376. The original FX primary uses a different historical window and lowers loss by 12.66%. The separately declared Treasury primary deteriorates by 50.79%, with 54 rather than 28 breaches. Short-history FX regression also deteriorates at the longer horizon; a Treasury neighbor gain reverses on the sparse grid. These adverse outcomes are central findings.

The paper makes three contributions. First, it places established forecasting engines and historical constructions on a common completed-peak response with an explicit issue-known floor. Second, it controls completed-label pools and update schedules and retains the complete favorable and adverse model menu. Third, it documents how score, breach frequency, report coherence and fixed-report preferences can disagree across two financial measurement processes. The contribution is an application and model-validation benchmark using mature methods.

Section 2 locates the study in the literature. Sections 3–5 describe data, forecasts and evaluation. Sections 6–7 report FX and Treasury results. Section 8 collects exploratory robustness evidence, Section 9 discusses mechanisms and limitations, and Section 10 concludes. Detailed historical menus, geometry and supplementary diagnostics appear in the appendices.

sections.title: 2. Related literature

blocks.html: Wisniewski, Lindsay and Lindsay (2020) and the net-position forecasting chapter of Wisniewski (2024) are the closest empirical lineage. They already study conditional, neighbor and normalized endpoint forecasts on the FX source family, using lagged positions and calendar information. Here the response is a single upper quantile of a future absolute sampled maximum, including the current magnitude. Marginal endpoint intervals and their averaged losses address a different functional; the present comparison fits the established engines directly to completed peak labels.

Financial path extrema have a substantial prior literature. MaxVaR evaluates worst intermediate mark-to-market loss (Boudoukh et al., 2004). Liao and Theodosopoulos (2005) study the timing of mark-to-market for collateralized contingent credit exposure. Van den Hoogen (2017) models a conditional intraday liquidity buffer through the maximum cumulative payment deficit; Petrunia, Sabetti and Voia (2019) study a cross-participant end-of-day debit maximum. Arjani, Li and Sabetti (2020) forecast remaining-day liquidity-demand ratios. These targets clarify the specific contribution of a sampled net-position envelope.

Regression quantiles (Koenker and Bassett, 1978), sequential neighbor quantiles (Biau and Patra, 2011), conditional historical filtering (Hull and White, 1998; Barone-Adesi et al., 1999), and quantile scoring (Gneiting, 2011) supply the mature methods. Quantile forests (Meinshausen, 2006), CAViaR (Engle and Manganelli, 2004), sequential conformal prediction (Xu and Xie, 2023), trajectory calibration (Zhou, Lindemann and Sesia, 2024) and expected-shortfall curves (Sözen, 2026) are further relevant alternatives. The executed estimator menu is deliberately bounded.

The resulting distinction is the measured peak response, known issue floor, completed-label timing, controlled history/update comparisons and qualified aggregate application. The benchmark measures how these mature procedures behave on the specified task; its supporting finite geometry explains construction differences.

sections.title: 3. Data

blocks.html: The FX input is the one-hour member of the Net Position Time Series Dataset, version 2: 18,576 records from 5 February 2014 01:00 through 24 January 2017 00:00. Wisniewski et al. (2020) describe aggregate client-flow positions across five liquid currency pairs for one market maker. We use datetime and the signed NetPosUsd scalar, rather than reconstructing raw currency positions, hedge transactions or cash movements. The source has 18,420 one-hour and 155 forty-nine-hour adjacent gaps. We preserve chronology without sorting, removing gap-crossing windows or interpolation. Recorded-clock and vintage limits are collected in Section 9.

The Treasury source is New York Fed Primary Dealer Statistics series PDPOSGS-B, Treasury-bill long positions less short positions. FR 2004A supplies Wednesday-close positions at market/fair value. Its instructions use trade-date accounting, with specified buyback treatment on settlement date, and include eligible forward and when-issued outright positions; the series is not settled cash holdings (Board of Governors, March 2013 and July 2024 instructions). The accepted snapshot has 706 seven-day-spaced records from 3 April 2013 through 7 October 2026, in USD millions. It aggregates reporting dealers and can reflect valuation or reporting-composition changes. Taking an absolute value after summing signed positions permits cross-dealer cancellation: a small aggregate can coexist with large individual magnitudes (Duffie et al., 2023). It does not identify gross exposures or pure customer order flow.

Treasury validation issue dates are 24 July 2019 to 15 July 2020. The final H=24 validation label ends at index 404 on 30 December 2020, before evaluation begins at 405 on 6 January 2021. The last common issue is 681 on 22 April 2026; its H=6 label ends at 687 on 3 June, and H=24 at 705 on 7 October 2026. FX validation ends at origin 11902; its latest H=24 label ends at 11926, before evaluation origin 11927.

The Treasury exercise is a downloaded-vintage replay indexed by economic as-of date, treating the current record as known at issue by convention. It is not a live public-information or as-released backtest.

sections.title: 5. Evaluation design

blocks.html: The FX primary is H6 QR W2880 minus original rolling F W720; the Treasury primary is H6 QR W260 minus frozen F W260. These are the two declared source-specific comparisons. The FX H24 QR W2880 minus original rolling S W720 comparison is a legacy-reference sensitivity: its reference was chosen in the preceding, already inspected study.

Every selected conditional family is compared with frozen F, S and K at matching source, horizon and history. The complete menu also retains rolling-versus-frozen update controls. The declared source primaries remain fixed throughout every post-result analysis.
Forecasts are scored in native source units using the stipulated upper-quantile pinball preference. The paired loss difference is left minus right, so a negative difference favors the left procedure:

e=P−C;   L<sub>.95</sub>=.95(e)<sub>+</sub>+.05(−e)<sub>+</sub>;   D=M<super>−1</super> ∑<sub>t</sub>[L(P<sub>t</sub>,C<sub>t</sub><super>left</super>)−L(P<sub>t</sub>,C<sub>t</sub><super>right</super>)].

The stipulated pinball score weights an underprediction dollar nineteen times an overprediction dollar. It is a consistent quantile score (Gneiting, 2011), rather than an observed financial cost. We report U=mean(P−C)<sub>+</sub>, the mean underprediction amount, and V=mean(C−P)<sub>+</sub>, the mean overprediction amount. Both average over all issue origins; conditional breach severity averages over each method's own strict P>C event set. The reported headroom C−B is distinct from V. Archived fields mean_positive_overrun, mean_unused_allowance and mean_extra_allowance correspond to U, V and mean(C−B); their historical names do not represent resources actually allocated. Lower mean loss and fewer breach occasions are separate outcomes. Financial units are never pooled across sources.

blocks.html: The H6 primary QR W2880 loss is USD 385,844.89, against USD 441,774.04 for original rolling F W720. The direct paired mean is −USD 55,929.15, or −12.660%. Against W2880 frozen F it is −14.767%; against frozen S at that same window it is also favorable. Thus the added conditional benchmark changes the older FX ranking. The cross-window primary changes history length and update frequency as well as the estimator; the matched-pool controls address these procedural differences while retaining estimator and feature distinctions.

The H6 score gain comes with more breach occasions. QR has 376 strict breaches (5.675%) versus 332 (5.011%) for old rolling F. Mean positive overrun falls from USD 166,531.06 to 156,123.03, while mean unused allowance falls by USD 920,830.41. More occasions breach, with a lower unconditional overrun contribution. Conditional severity averages different method-specific event sets; the statistic therefore compares different incident compositions. At W720, H6 QR improves on frozen F by only 2.117%, while scaled KNN is worse by 5.349%.

At H24, QR W2880 loss is USD 734,695.07 against USD 748,383.54 for old rolling S W720: −USD 13,688.47 (−1.829%). Breaches increase from 287 (4.332%) to 531 (8.015%); mean positive overrun rises from USD 149,813.88 to 317,678.12, while unused allowance falls. With W720, QR instead loses to frozen F by 31.504% and frozen S by 37.095%. In the inspected FX record, the H24 regression ranking changes with the history window.

The H6 primary loss difference is negative in both issue-year groups: −12.012% over 6,262 origins in 2016 and −29.513% over the 363-origin partial 2017. The latter contains 5.48% of all issue origins and contributes 8.64% of the H6 primary net gain and 6.87% of the matched-history H6 net gain. For both H6 comparisons, U and V fall in each issue-year group and on the fixed 947-origin grid. In contrast, H24 improves against its legacy reference by only 0.555% in 2016 and 33.007% in partial 2017; 70.83% of its small total net gain comes from that short tail segment, and U increases in both groups and on the 265-origin grid. Figure 3 shows the issue-year contrasts. The fixed H+1 grids retain favorable H6/H24 legacy-reference loss differences of −16.388%/−8.027%. These are decompositions and sensitivities of the same inspected record, not independent validation or a basis for retrospective forecast switching.

sections.title: 8. Robustness

blocks.html: AR has lower loss in five of eight cells against S, five against F and five against QR; these sets differ. Relative to QR it loses in three of four FX cells and improves in all four Treasury cells. The exploratory AR comparisons show a different observed loss pattern from the adverse Treasury QR primary. Against S, the FX H6 changes are −1.536%/−0.546% at W720/W2880, while H24 changes are +2.386%/+5.147%. Treasury changes are −13.444%/−18.887% at H6 and +35.125%/−24.118% at H24 for W52/W260. The complete table retains the original model identities. Against S, AR mean report and mean unused allowance decrease in every cell, while strict breach occasions increase in all eight and mean positive overrun increases in seven. Treasury H24 W260 loss falls from 2478.871 to 1881.016 USD millions (−24.118%), yet breaches rise from 12 to 59 of 277 and mean positive overrun rises from 306.848 to 892.437. Mean unused allowance falls from 43747.307 to 20664.031. Under the stipulated score, .05 times the unused reduction exceeds .95 times the added overrun. This explains the observed loss change without asserting safer limits, calibrated tails or observed financing savings.

A later post-inspection rank/endpoint ablation adds a same-pool, same-update intercept-only empirical headroom quantile, choosing its lower minimizer endpoint. The matched FX H6 W2880 QR comparison still lowers loss by 14.773%, with 376 rather than 365 breaches; the matched Treasury H6 W260 QR comparison still raises loss by 46.058%, with 54 rather than 32 breaches. All four Treasury QR cells remain adverse against this added report. The lower-rank rule improves on original frozen F in three cells and loses in five, so the empirical minimizer endpoint can perform worse in evaluation. The two headline signs persist under this specific control. Table D3 retains every cell and the later design history.

Within each source/H/W cell, the lower envelope is computed only over eight archived .95 reports: QR, KNN, scaled KNN, matched frozen F/S/K, AR and I. They share the completed-label history length and refit schedule, but this finite menu does not exhaust feasible reports. For example, C=B is feasible and has V=0, making it a minimizer at a=0 over all feasible reports; that floor-only action is absent from this eight-report menu. The reported endpoint winners therefore describe the menu, rather than all feasible decisions. Rolling and one-state reports are also excluded; the original cross-window primary references are separately labeled in Table 6. Appendix E retains all full and sparse-grid envelopes, endpoints and ties. Full-grid Treasury H6 W260 QR is never optimal among these eight reports, including both endpoints. At a=.95 the menu minimizer changes on four of eight sparse grids: FX H24 W720, Treasury H6 W52/W260 and Treasury H24 W52. Treasury H24 grids contain only 12 origins. These are dependent within-archive sensitivities, rather than four independent replication outcomes.

Post-result diagnostics clarify the issued reports rather than changing their rankings. Every common realized target satisfies P(H6)≤P(H24), yet the separately fitted reports can cross: FX W720 QR crosses on 640/6,625 issues, and Treasury W52 QR on 91/277. Some short Treasury historical F/S controls also cross because the horizons use different mature episode sets. Appendix D retains all 45 original pairs and a separately frozen addition covering all four AR pairs. AR has zero observed FX crossings, but Treasury W52/W260 cross on 59/26 of 277 issues. The horizon-specific fits and mature scenario sets differ, producing the observed incoherence. Figure 3 retains the complete annual comparison; all detailed coherence and fixed-terminal diagnostics remain in Appendix D.

Consequently neither report empirically dominates the other over the entire class of consistent 0.95-quantile scores. The check evaluates every unique forecast/outcome breakpoint privately; the displayed 201-point grid is an aggregate visualization. A cost per breach or a nonlinear loss can therefore change the ranking. The smaller H24 FX legacy gain instead trades increased U for reduced V and reverses at ratio 20.63. sections.title: 9. Discussion and limitations

blocks.text: Feature transport and the Treasury failure

blocks.html: The executed QR specifications perform poorly on the weekly Treasury task. Their 25 level coordinates span the current observation through 24 weeks of history. The two hour coordinates, two weekday coordinates and gap indicator are exactly constant on this weekly source. Training-only centering makes those five columns exactly zero, so they provide no predictive variation and are not a demonstrated mechanism of overfitting. The original nominal design has 33 predictors plus an intercept, or 34 coefficients, with at most 28 varying columns and 29 potentially predictive coefficients before other collinearity, against W=52 overlapping training labels in the shorter history. All four Treasury penalty selections are menu endpoints. Its 52 validation origins contain at most 3 disjoint H24 label paths, a path count rather than an effective-sample-size estimate. Correlated lag levels, overlapping labels, restricted tuning, target dynamics and reporting composition remain competing explanations. Neither the parsimonious sensitivity nor the aggregate panel separates those mechanisms.

The four-predictor sensitivity uses B, signed N and short/long increment RMS, with validation penalties {0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10}. It lowers loss against the original QR in 5 of 8 cells and against matched F in 3 cells. In the Treasury primary cell its loss change is -32.2% relative to the original QR and 2.17% relative to F. All adverse cells remain in Table 8. The exercise changes features and the penalty menu jointly, so it measures a parsimonious specification sensitivity rather than identifying a feature-only cause or rehabilitating the original primary.

The contrast between the sources concerns a separately fitted procedure family: each source receives its own transforms, coefficient estimates, temporal scales and validation selection. The Treasury deterioration is an accuracy failure of the executed QR specifications. The exploratory AR comparison shows that the observed Treasury loss ranking differs across the executed families.

The FX evaluation interval was previously inspected, and the subsequent robustness analyses are post-result / exploratory. These records do not restore a compatible unseen dealer sample. Treasury is a downloaded-vintage, economic-date aggregate replay rather than an original-release public-information backtest; cross-dealer netting, valuation and composition distinguish it from an individual dealer's book.

Shared histories, overlapping labels, finite validation and investigator selection limit statistical generalization. The known floor can create an outcome atom: a valid upper quantile need not have exactly the nominal strict-breach probability. Numerical acceptance supplies no conditional-coverage guarantee. The horizon-specific mature scenario sets differ, so a zero observed crossing count cannot establish general coherence.

Stipulated shortfall/excess weights are not observed financing prices. Quotes, fills, hedges, book decomposition, collateral and cash flows would be required to map this passive envelope into an operational inventory, margin or funding policy. This study evaluates forecasts, not such interventions; Avellaneda and Stoikov (2008) provide a distinct active inventory-sensitive quoting framework.

Further alternatives include CAViaR, sequential conformal procedures, richer mean or volatility dynamics, and canonical innovation-tail conditional EVT. The fixed FHS, QRF and peak-POT additions in Appendix L extend the executed menu, with their failures and resource bounds retained. Same mature-label pools and update schedules improve procedural comparability while leaving different feature lookbacks, model assumptions and estimation rules. Compatible new dealer observations and decision-linked inputs remain necessary for broader portability.

A post-result / exploratory selected-fit readback examines the Treasury C2 menu boundary directly (Appendix I). At λ=10, standardized response-normalized slope norms range from 0.001497 to 0.01937. Removing slopes while keeping each fitted intercept changes capacity by a mean absolute 136.8–832.3 source USD millions across the four cells. Relative to the lower empirical headroom-quantile report I, observed loss is 0.2432–2.192% lower; this descriptive difference has no dedicated selection-adjusted test. The fits have small normalized slopes and high headroom correlation with I, but are not identical to I or F. A boundary penalty and high capacity correlation do not by themselves demonstrate zero feature value. Three of the four C2 cells still have higher loss than F.

The expanded aggregate panel strengthens the negative transport finding but does not isolate its mechanism. Features and tuning menus, finite sample size, target behavior and reporting-regime changes can all matter. Downloaded cross-era histories are not original-release vintages; metadata/provenance for each key are retained. A prospective public-release protocol freezes the four procedures and selected historical-validation penalties before future issue artifacts. The first planned new release is after the protocol freeze, rather than retroactively labeling the already published October 14 observation as unseen. Because the release clock lags economic dates, the target includes prediction of unpublished measurements, with a nowcast/forecast mixture. A dated local amendment fixes future path values at their first actual capture and logs later revisions separately; operational capture and missing-week handling still require a bound adapter (Appendix K). Results await prior timestamped report issuance and target publication; no live prospective validation is claimed.

sections.title: 10. Conclusion

blocks.html: Mature conditional estimators change the historical ranking on the sampled FX peak task, while the Treasury regression primary deteriorates. Matched-history FX H6 QR lowers mean loss by 14.77% and raises breaches from 360 to 376; the Treasury primary raises loss by 50.79% and breaches from 28 to 54. Short-history QR deterioration and the sparse-grid Treasury neighbor reversal remain central adverse findings. The exploratory AR, rank, preference and coherence comparisons show why score improvements, breach frequency and report shape should be evaluated together. The study contributes a controlled application and model-validation benchmark for measured position peaks. Its next evidential step is compatible new financial observations and an explicit decision mapping.
The exploratory 12-series extension also finds higher loss than F in 45/48 QR33 cells and 37/48 parsimonious cells, further limiting general performance claims.

Fixed FHS, peak-POT and leaf-distribution QRF add adverse outcomes and explicit numerical exclusions rather than a universal accuracy ranking. Compatible unseen-dealer evidence remains an open requirement.

These statements do not automatically bound QR, scaled responses or the richer 33-coordinate distance.

A training-only RMS conditions the fit numerically. A single optimization is allowed; failures remain NA. The coefficients and standardized residual pool are frozen between refits; newly observed increments update the variance state through issue t. In-sample historical filtered volatilities estimated at κ are not historical forecasts made at i. Finite fitted recursion and optimizer termination supply no independence, stationarity or coverage guarantee.

The subscript G marks local GARCH coefficients, distinguishing them from the regression intercept and fixed-report preference ratio used elsewhere. The POT shape and scale below carry hats and refer to a separate tail fit.

FHS draws 2048 iid residual paths with replacement, using a seed bound to source, H, W and κ; draws are shared within that refit block. Each path recursively updates GARCH variance and signed increments from actual N<sub>t</sub>. Its simulated maximum includes h=0, and the empirical headroom quantile uses rank ⌈19(M+1)/20⌉. The fitted mean equation is constant; resampling retains the stored standardized residuals without further empirical recentering or rescaling, so their finite resampling distribution need not have exactly zero mean or unit variance. This is a same-target adaptation, rather than an exact replica of the original derivative-portfolio application.

McNeil and Frey (2000) fit tails of filtered one-step return innovations and simulate multi-period sums. The present headroom-tail scaling is not that original procedure. Dependence on the signed anchor relative to volatility, drift and the future variance path remains after a single-scale normalization; overlapping mature labels remain dependent. These are substantive approximation limits, not cured by successful GPD optimization.

The forest uses the same 33 causal predictors, training-only transforms and response scaling as QR. The fixed 100-tree regression partitions have max_features=11, minimum leaf 5, split 10, maximum depth 10, bootstrap enabled and one worker. All original training rows receive within-leaf mass, averaged over trees; bootstrap chooses partitions but does not multiply these CDF masses. The left inverse at 0.95 selects a positive-mass training response with no interpolation or F rank correction. This bounded fixed configuration is not claimed to optimize QRF or transfer the original consistency theorem to dependent fixed-window data.
